text: Before we write a single line of code, what actually happens when someone pays a shop online with a card?

text: Five players are involved: the buyer, the shop, the acquirer bank, the processing center, and the issuer bank.
prefix: Five players are involved: the buyer, the shop, the acquirer bank, the processing center, and the issuer bank.

text: The acquirer is the shop's bank, the one we are building, and the issuer is the bank that gave the buyer their card.

text: Every shop gets a terminal at the acquirer, identified by a merchant ID and a terminal ID, the MID and TID.

text: When the buyer pays, the acquirer sends an authorization through the processing center to the issuer.

text: The issuer checks the balance and places a hold, so the money is reserved but not yet moved.

text: Then the acquirer captures the hold, and the payment becomes final.

text: A reversal cancels a payment before settlement, and a refund sends money back after it.

text: At the end of the day, the processing center settles all payments with the acquirer.

text: The acquirer keeps its commission and pays the shop the rest by the next banking day.
